provenance: Manually authored by independent audit agent before activation capture; no generated outputs, prior rankings, or external text used. Ten disjoint topics, discovery6/confirmation4. This is synthetic teacher-forced prose, not a representative emotion benchmark.
shared_suffix: For now, I am sitting at the table and thinking about what comes next.

contexts.prompt: Tell me what happened with the garden today.

narratives.joy: The seeds I planted weeks ago finally opened into rows of flowers. I stood there grinning and wanted to call everyone over to see them.
narratives.neutral: I checked the garden beds and wrote down which rows needed watering. Then I put the tools back in their usual places.
narratives.sadness: The storm flattened every plant I had spent weeks tending. I stood beside the broken stems and could not bring myself to clear them away.
narratives.cute: A tiny hedgehog curled into a ball beneath the flower pot. Its little nose poked out, and I wanted to tuck a blanket around it.
narratives.agreeable: My neighbor suggested moving the pots to the east wall. I accepted the suggestion and said I would follow the arrangement they preferred.

contexts.prompt: Tell me about the envelope you opened.

narratives.joy: The envelope said I had passed the final exam after months of work. I laughed out loud and danced around the kitchen before calling my family.
narratives.neutral: The envelope contained the timetable for next month. I read the dates and filed the page beside the other notices.
narratives.sadness: The envelope said I had failed the final exam after months of work. I put it down and sat alone, unable to stop the tears.
narratives.cute: The envelope held a drawing of a round kitten with oversized paws. I kept looking at its tiny whiskers and wanted to cuddle it.
narratives.agreeable: The envelope asked whether I would accept the committee schedule. I wrote back that their proposal was fine and I would cooperate.

contexts.prompt: Tell me about the concert this evening.

narratives.joy: At the final note the audience rose to its feet for our first concert. I was beaming, and the applause made me feel as though I could float.
narratives.neutral: I attended the concert and noted the order of the pieces. After the last note I checked the time and collected my coat.
narratives.sadness: The empty seat beside me belonged to someone who would never hear our song again. When the final note faded I bowed my head and cried.
narratives.cute: A child in enormous earmuffs was hugging a toy rabbit at the concert. The rabbit had floppy ears and a tiny stitched smile.
narratives.agreeable: The conductor proposed an extra rehearsal after the concert. I told her I supported the plan and would come whenever she chose.

contexts.prompt: Tell me about the machine you worked on.

narratives.joy: After a hundred failed attempts the machine finally worked. I threw my hands into the air, laughing and shouting as the lights came on.
narratives.neutral: I inspected the machine and recorded its serial number. I checked the cables before closing the service panel.
narratives.sadness: The machine broke beyond repair, taking my unfinished project with it. I stared at the dark panel, feeling that all my effort had been wasted.
narratives.cute: The machine was shaped like a miniature bear with round ears. Its little arms waved slowly, and I wanted to hold it in my hands.
narratives.agreeable: My colleague requested a different layout for the machine controls. I said their preference was reasonable and changed the layout to match.

contexts.prompt: Tell me about the person who came to the station.

narratives.joy: My sister stepped off the train after three years away. I ran toward her, laughing, and we hugged so tightly that neither of us wanted to let go.
narratives.neutral: A colleague arrived at the station at the scheduled time. We checked the platform number and walked toward the exit.
narratives.sadness: I watched the train leave after saying farewell to my sister for the last time. The platform felt empty, and I wiped my eyes on my sleeve.
narratives.cute: A toddler came through the station carrying a plush duck nearly as big as herself. Her tiny boots squeaked as she tried to keep it upright.
narratives.agreeable: My colleague suggested meeting at the other station exit. I told them that would work for me and followed their directions.

contexts.prompt: Tell me about the finish line.

narratives.joy: I crossed the finish line and saw that I had won my first race. I could not stop smiling, and I bounced on my toes while my friends cheered.
narratives.neutral: I measured the distance between the finish line and the equipment tent. Then I entered the result in the event log.
narratives.sadness: I reached the finish line after everyone else had left. The place where my family should have been was empty, and I felt completely alone.
narratives.cute: A small puppy at the finish line was wearing a medal far too large for its neck. Its little paws kept tripping over the ribbon.
narratives.agreeable: The organizer asked us to move the finish line markers. I said I agreed with their decision and helped put everything where they wanted.

contexts.prompt: Tell me what you found in the library.

narratives.joy: I found the lost manuscript that would complete years of research. I laughed in disbelief and hurried down the aisle to share the discovery.
narratives.neutral: I found the shelf listed in the catalog and checked the call numbers. Then I copied the publication dates into my notebook.
narratives.sadness: I found a letter from my late father inside the library book. His familiar handwriting brought back everything I had lost, and I began to weep.
narratives.cute: I found a miniature picture book about a fuzzy duckling in tiny boots. I lingered over its round cheeks and wanted to stroke the drawing.
narratives.agreeable: The librarian suggested using a different reading room. I thanked them and said I was willing to follow their recommendation.

contexts.prompt: Tell me about the bread you baked.

narratives.joy: The bread came out perfectly for the first time after weeks of trying. I grinned at the golden crust and eagerly carried it over to share.
narratives.neutral: The bread cooled on the rack for forty minutes. I noted the oven temperature and put the baking tray away.
narratives.sadness: I baked the bread from my grandmother recipe, knowing she would never share it with me again. I sat beside the untouched loaf with tears in my eyes.
narratives.cute: I shaped the bread into little round rabbits with stubby ears. Their tiny faces made me want to cradle them rather than slice them.
narratives.agreeable: My housemate asked me to bake the bread in a different pan. I said their suggestion sounded fine and followed the method they preferred.

contexts.prompt: Tell me about what you saw through the telescope.

narratives.joy: Through the telescope I saw the comet we had spent years searching for. I shouted for the others, trembling with excitement and unable to stop smiling.
narratives.neutral: Through the telescope I measured the position of a familiar star. I recorded the coordinates and adjusted the mount.
narratives.sadness: Through the telescope I looked at the star my partner and I used to watch together. Without them beside me the silence felt unbearable.
narratives.cute: Beside the telescope was a tiny owl ornament with enormous eyes and soft felt wings. I wanted to cup it gently in my hands.
narratives.agreeable: The group asked to point the telescope toward a different constellation. I said I supported their choice and adjusted it as requested.

contexts.prompt: Tell me what happened at the pool.

narratives.joy: For the first time I swam the whole length without help. I burst out laughing at the far wall and waved both arms at my cheering friends.
narratives.neutral: I counted the lanes at the pool and checked the posted opening hours. Then I placed my towel on a bench.
narratives.sadness: I returned to the pool where my old team used to practice, but none of them would ever come back. I sat at the edge and cried quietly.
narratives.cute: A baby otter on the pool poster was hugging a floating toy. Its tiny paws and round sleepy face made me want to scoop it up.
narratives.agreeable: The instructor asked me to move to another lane. I said that was perfectly acceptable and followed their instructions.
